title: Global-section matrices and ordinary internal scalar extension on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, small in a universe admitting abelian sheafification and the tensor product of abelian sheaves, with final object $1$, and suppose the internal/sectionwise module equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] applies. Let $R,S$ be commutative ring objects in abelian sheaves, let $\psi:R\to S$ be a ring-object morphism, and put $A=\Gamma(1,R)$, $B=\Gamma(1,S)$, $\varphi=\Gamma(1,\psi):A\to B$. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and ordinary coequalizer scalar extension [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For every $m,n\geq0$ there is a canonical additive bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_R(R^{\oplus n},R^{\oplus m})\cong M_{m\times n}(A).$$
A matrix $T=(t_{ij})$ acts on sections at $U$ by $(a_j)_j\mapsto(\sum_j(t_{ij}|_U)a_j)_i$; its entries are uniquely the global components of the images of the standard basis sections. The bijections send composition to matrix multiplication and identities to identity matrices. There are canonical isomorphisms
$$S\otimes_R R^{\oplus n}\cong S^{\oplus n},\qquad (b\otimes(a_j)_j)\longmapsto(b\psi(a_j))_j,$$
whose inverse on a section $(b_j)_j$ is $\sum_j b_j\otimes e_j$, interpreted in the sheaf tensor product. Under these isomorphisms scalar extension of the morphism with matrix $T$ has matrix $(\varphi(t_{ij}))$. The coefficient-unit map is induced by $\psi$ on each section ring. Both Hom sets are singleton zero groups when $m=0$ or $n=0$, and extension preserves rank zero. These are identities for internal sheaf tensor products; no equality between tensor products of section rings and sections of arbitrary tensor products is asserted.

source.place: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Example 3.1, p. 6; elementary global-basis calculation and explicit balanced-map calculation for ordinary internal coequalizer scalar extension. Returned item proof steps 8 and 10, stated for a general ringed site.

proof.text: Use the canonical finite biproduct projections on each section group, with inverse the sum of the biproduct inclusions. The biproduct total identity and inclusion-projection identities prove these additive equivalences are inverse, including the empty index set. No comparison of tensor sections with tensors of sections is needed.

By the underlying-section-preserving functor of def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence, a map between regular internal modules is linear on sections. Naturality along the unique U to one and linearity give f_U(a) = restriction(f_one(1)) a. Conversely multiplication by the restrictions of a global section defines a sectionwise linear natural map, which full faithfulness lifts to an internal module map. Evaluation at one on 1 and the displayed formula prove these assignments are inverse.

Define the (i,j) matrix entry by evaluating inclusion_j then f then projection_i on 1 at the terminal object. Its inverse is biproduct.matrix of the regular-module maps constructed in step 2. The two biproduct extensionality lemmas prove inverse identities; addition is entrywise. Decomposing a section by the biproduct total identity and applying step 2 gives the section formula. Evaluation on a basis vector then proves composition is matrix multiplication, and the inclusion-projection identities give the identity matrix.

For rank one use the right-unitor isomorphism of the S-R bimodule Bimod.ofMonHom psi. Its defining coequalizer desc has composite with extendPi equal to S tensor psi followed by multiplication, and its inverse inserts the unit of R. The local tensor generator naturality and the reconstructed section-ring multiplication give the local formula b tensor a maps to b psi(a). The extension unit followed by this isomorphism is psi by the unitor and monoid unit laws.

Scalar extension is a left adjoint, hence preserves finite biproducts. Define theta_n as its mapBiproduct comparison followed by the biproduct of the rank-one isomorphisms. Composing with projection_j gives extension(projection_j) then the rank-one comparison. The extendPi map formula, lax tensor generator naturality, and step 4 prove the specified local pure-tensor formula in every coordinate. Naturality of the extension unit and step 4 similarly give the coordinatewise unit formula.

Apply theta_n to the proposed inverse sum. Additivity and the local tensor formula of step 5 give, in coordinate i, sum_j b_j psi(delta_ji) = b_i. Cancel the sectionwise isomorphism to obtain the inverse formula on every tuple. The unit formula also shows theta_n inverse sends a standard S-basis vector to the extension unit on the corresponding R-basis vector. Naturality of that unit now computes the conjugated extended arrow on each basis vector, yielding psi(t_ij).

The rank-zero biproduct has identity zero by biproduct extensionality over Fin 0, hence is zero. A zero source or target makes the corresponding Hom group subsingleton, and a matrix with an empty dimension is subsingleton. Transport zero along theta_0 to prove scalar extension preserves rank zero. None of the calculations requires nonzero rings or flatness.
